mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a weakening economy, leading to negative investor sentiment and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when GDPC1 drops > 1% QoQ, or if the correlation between GDPC1 growth and 60-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals labor market distress, leading to negative investor sentiment and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5%, or if the correlation between UNRATE changes and 5-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over three months signals a strong supply-side response, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO rises > 2%, or if the correlation between INDPRO growth and 20-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 5% month-over-month signals strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances when RSAFS rises > 5%, or if the correlation between RSAFS growth and 5-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% over three months signals an easing monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS drops > 0.5%, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS changes and 60-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 5% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) decreases by more than 100,000 in a month, it signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE > 5% and PAYEMS drops > 100k, or if the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS changes on 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decrease by more than 10% month-over-month and CPI (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals a demand-side shock, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST drops > 10% MoM and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% MoM
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST drops > 10% MoM and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% MoM, or if the joint effect of HOUST and CPIAUCSL changes on 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).
